in_arabic.name: مهرز
in_arabic.meaning: المهرز اسم يعني السحر والحرفة والذواقة

She is best known for her beauty, intelligence, and her tragic love story with Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni. Sultan Mahmud fell deeply in love with her and went to great lengths to win her heart, even proposing to her multiple times. However, Mehruz rejected him due to her deep devotion to her father and her unwillingness to betray him. In frustration, Mahmud attacked and destroyed Ghazni, killing Mehruz's father and brothers. Unable to bear the loss and the guilt of her father's death, Mehruz took her own life.

Mehruz was also the name of a famous Sufi saint who lived during the 14th century in India. She was a disciple of Baba Farid, a prominent Sufi poet and saint. Mehruz is known for her deep spiritual devotion and her remarkable asceticism. She lived a simple life, dedicating herself to the service of God. Her life and teachings have been a source of inspiration for many Sufis and mystics in India and beyond.
